verdict.rationale: Gusto's official remote MCP server uses an OAuth2 connection flow that lets the user choose which categories of data the connected LLM can access, which is a product-native way to grant an agent scoped, least-privilege access. The evidence for this is a single docs summary, and scoping is limited to per-connection data categories rather than documented fine-grained credential issuance. missing for 10: documented granular scope definitions such as read-only versus write or per-endpoint permissions, credential lifecycle controls like revocation, expiry and rotation for agent connections, scoped token issuance outside the MCP connection flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Our MCP server provides an OAuth2 based connection process and allows you to select the categories of data to which your chosen LLM will have access.
